title: fix(metadata-protocol): diagnostics stop flagging `picklist` and `options` on a field that declares only `picklist`
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XQiacasSoJzxf6CYy6p4JTT)_

Fixes #26886

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：字段只写了 `picklist`（共享选项列表）时，元数据诊断（Setup › 所有元数据类型的问题数、条目 `_diagnostics`、`GET /meta/diagnostics`）不再误报「`picklist` 和 `options` 不能同时声明」。真正同时写了两个键的字段照报，文案和级别不变。
- **为什么改**：运行时把共享列表的选项解析到字段上再下发，诊断却校验了这份解析后的副本，于是每个用共享选项列表的应用（HotCRM 有 11 个字段）都给管理员亮红色错误，说应用坏了，实际选择框工作正常。
- **风险与回滚**：低。`/meta/object/:name` 下发内容不变（仍是 `picklist` + 解析后的 `options`），规则本身不动。新增的只是 picklist 解析在它生成的 options 数组上打一个不可枚举的标记，诊断见标记才略过；标记丢失时退回旧行为（误报），不会漏报。回滚即 revert。
- **先看**：`packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts`（`withoutResolvedPicklistOptions`）；`packages/objectql/src/picklist-resolution.ts`（`resolveField` 打标记的条件）；`packages/metadata-core/src/resolved-picklist-options.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/protocol-picklist-served-roundtrip.test.ts`，预期 4/4 通过，其中三入口用例只报 `fields.both.options` 一条。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

The global-picklist resolution in `@objectstack/objectql` (`resolveField` in `picklist-resolution.ts`) now marks the `options` array it derives for a field that names a picklist, and the load-time diagnostics in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (`computeMetadataDiagnostics`) leave a marked array out of the document before the schema parse. A field is therefore judged as its author wrote it:

| Field as authored | Served by `GET /meta/object/:name` | Diagnostic before | Diagnostic after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `picklist: 'industry'` | `picklist` + resolved `options` | "`picklist` and `options` cannot both be declared" | clean |
| `picklist` and its own `options` | `picklist` + resolved `options` | flagged | flagged, same message and severity, at `fields.NAME.options` |
| inline `options` only | unchanged | clean | clean |

- **When the resolution marks.** Only when the body it resolves carried no `options`, or carried options that are themselves marked (a served copy re-folded in memory). A body that brought unmarked `options` beside `picklist` is an authored pair and its resolved options stay unmarked, so the rule still fires.
- **The mark.** `markResolvedPicklistOptions` / `isResolvedPicklistOptions`, a new module in `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`resolved-picklist-options.ts`): a non-enumerable property keyed with `Symbol.for`, on the array itself. It is not in any response, stored row, JSON or memo key; every loaded copy of the package reads the one key. A copy of the array (`.map`, spread, JSON round trip) does not carry it, so a reader of a copy reports the diagnostic: the failure direction is the old false error, never a missed one.
- **Why `metadata-core`.** Both sides already declare it. The resolution sits in the lean `@objectstack/objectql/core` closure, which must not import `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (ADR-0076 D2; `core-boundary.ratchet.test.ts` and `check:lean-entry-closure` both refused the first version of this PR, which put the mark in `metadata-protocol`).
- **Unchanged.** The rule itself (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, untouched); what `/meta` serves; the save door (a PUT of the served body is still refused 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, pinned by the existing test in `protocol-picklist-served-roundtrip.test.ts`). No second copy of the rule.

### Doors that show the diagnostic, all through the one seam

`computeMetadataDiagnostics` is the only place the read side parses an item, so every door below is fixed by the one change:

1. An item read's `_diagnostics` (`getMetaItem` → `decorateMetadataItem`).
2. A list read's per-item `_diagnostics` (`getMetaItems` → `decorateMetadataItems`).
3. `GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics` (`protocol-meta-diagnostics.ts` reads the list's `_diagnostics`, or computes it), which is what Setup › All Metadata Types counts.
4. The layered read's `_diagnostics` on the effective item (`protocol.ts`, `getMetaItemLayers`).

The boot-time scan of stored `sys_metadata` rows (`protocol.ts`, `convertStoredItem` → `computeMetadataDiagnostics`) parses the stored body, which is authored and never resolved, so it is unmarked and keeps flagging a stored row that carries both keys.

## Why

Seat ruling on the card: judge what the author wrote, never the resolved copy; "If the resolved shape is the only thing that pass can see, the resolution may mark what it derived." Measured which applies: the authored item is not visible at the decoration seam.

- Every object read folds through the registry's `finishServedObject` (`foldObjectExtendersOnto` / `resolveObject`) before decoration, and that fold resolves the picklist.
- The MetadataService body the item read prefers can itself be a served copy: the boot bridge copies `registry.getAllObjects()` (resolved bodies) into the service.
- `resolveField` overwrites a field's `options` unconditionally, so even an authored pair reaches the decoration seam with the picklist's options: the served copy alone cannot tell the two apart.

So the resolution marks what it derived. Stripping every `options` beside `picklist` in the diagnostics instead would silence an authored pair on every door: a consumer-side tolerance the ruling excludes.

## Tests

- `metadata-core` `resolved-picklist-options.test.ts` (new, 4): the mark is in place and only on the marked array, invisible to JSON and key enumeration, gone from any copy of the array, kept through a copy of the field holding it.
- `metadata-protocol` `metadata-diagnostics.resolved-picklist-options.test.ts` (new, 6): picklist-only field served with marked options is clean; an authored pair is flagged at `fields.industry.options` with the rule's message; inline-only clean; a marked array on a field with no `picklist` is judged as written; a marked and an unmarked document with the same JSON are two verdicts in either order (the verdict memo); the decorated item keeps both keys and no trace of the mark.
- `objectql` `protocol-picklist-served-roundtrip.test.ts` (+2): a real `ObjectQL` registry with a code-registered object (picklist-only `industry`, inline `stage`, authored pair `both`) through `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`: the item read, the list read and `getMetaDiagnostics` each report exactly `fields.both.options`; the item read still serves `industry` with `picklist` and the resolved options.

<details><summary>Red first, ablation</summary>

- Red on `main` (`57820085`), same harness as the new objectql test, before any edit: the item read, the list read and `getMetaDiagnostics` each reported `fields.industry.options` "`picklist` and `options` cannot both be declared" for a field declaring only `picklist`.
- Ablation (committed fix): in `picklist-resolution.ts`, `markResolvedPicklistOptions(resolved);` replaced by `void 0;` (on disk: 0 of the first, 1 of the second) turned both new objectql tests red (2 failed, 2 passed: the authored-pair control and the existing round-trip tests stay green). Restored from HEAD; `git diff HEAD` empty afterwards.

</details>

<details><summary>Live check (os dev)</summary>

`examples/app-todo` with its `category` field switched to `picklist: 'todo_category'` and a matching `picklists` entry (a scratch edit, not committed; restored), booted with `os dev --fresh`, signed in as the seeded admin:

| | `main` metadata-protocol + objectql (base blobs rebuilt) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /meta/diagnostics?type=object` | 1 entry: `todo_task` `fields.category.options` "`picklist` and `options` cannot both be declared" | 0 entries |
| `GET /meta/diagnostics` (all types, 177 items) | total 1 | total 0 |
| `GET /meta/object/todo_task` `fields.category` | `picklist: "todo_category"` + 5 resolved `options` | identical |
| `todo_task._diagnostics` | `valid: false` (that one error) | `valid: true` |

The count drops by exactly the false row. Base blobs were restored and both packages rebuilt from HEAD afterwards.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **HotCRM path not booted.** The card's own reproduction is HotCRM on published 18.2.0. The live check above uses the in-repo `app-todo` with the same field shape (a code package's object naming a picklist); booting HotCRM against this branch's packages was not done.
- **A copy loses the mark.** Any future step between the fold and the decoration that copies a field's `options` array (rather than the field) would bring the false error back for that door, loudly and in the safe direction. Today no step does: the item, list and sweep doors and the live boot all read clean.

## Verification

All at head `a6f469a3`, after the final commit:

- Package suites (under the verify lock): `@objectstack/objectql` test: Test Files 475 passed (475), Tests 8851 passed; `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` test: Test Files 274 passed, 4 skipped (278), Tests 21699 passed, 26 skipped; `@objectstack/metadata-core` test: Test Files 21 passed, Tests 840 passed. `typecheck` of all three: exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the seven touched `.ts` files: exit 0.
- Derived gate families (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`): 62 derived, 62 run, every one exit 0; `--ran` reconciliation: "62 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED". `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was read after a full `pnpm build` (it reads every package's `dist/`): 112 require entry points across 69 packages load. `check:lean-entry-closure` and `core-boundary.ratchet.test.ts` are green on this head (both were red on the first version, which imported `metadata-protocol` into the lean core closure).
- Not run locally, owned by CI: `test:repo`, the repo-wide `pnpm lint`, and the families outside the derived list.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (No `packages/spec` change.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. (`eslint --no-inline-config` on the touched files, exit 0.)
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (Not touched.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
